In Aldergrove, Langley, the 55+ homes you can buy are Creekside Villa and Pioneer Park (strata and manufactured-home park). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is retirement residence or care. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Aldergrove

A gated 55+ rancher townhouse complex, freehold strata, plan LMS361, built 1992, 55 units. MLS property data records "Age Restrictions, Pets Allowed w/Rest., Age Restricted 55+", adult-oriented community features, and a legal description under strata plan LMS361; listings describe a "55+ rancher in a gated community backing onto peaceful Bertrand Creek" and a one-level rancher townhouse form with a double garage. Pets: listings state 2 pets maximum with a shoulder-height limit — confirm the current pet bylaw in the Form B.
Pioneer Park — 27111 0 Ave (Aldergrove, at the US border)

A 55+ manufactured-home co-operative. MLS listings for homes in the park state "Pioneer Park is 55+", that both occupants must be 55 in one listing's wording ("Strictly 55plus (both occupants must be 55)"), and that a buyer must be accepted by the co-op and purchase co-op shares — one listing states shares of $9,200, refunded upon sale, with $510/month co-op fees and 2 pets allowed with no size restrictions. Those dollar figures are listing-stated for specific homes at specific dates — confirm the current share price, monthly co-op fee and occupancy rule with the co-op before writing. This is neither a strata purchase nor a standard pad-rental park: the land is held through the co-operative.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Aldergrove (not for sale)

items.t: Jackman Manor — 27477 28 Ave (Aldergrove): A long-term care home for elders, owned and operated by the Aldergrove Lions Seniors Housing Society, opened 1982. The Seniors Advocate records 88 beds as of March 31, 2025, all publicly funded, in single-occupancy rooms. Fraser Health describes it as care for elders who can no longer live safely or independently at home due to complex health care needs. Long-term care is accessed through Fraser Health, not purchased.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Aldergrove

items.t: Aldergrove is a community in the Township of Langley; the Township states its eastern boundary is 276 Street bordering the City of Abbotsford and its southern boundary is the United States border.

The Aldergrove Core Area is centred on Fraser Highway and 272 Street, bounded by Bertrand Creek to the north and east, 29 Avenue to the south and 270 Street to the west; wider community boundaries are UNVERIFIED.

The two verified 55+ ownership complexes sit in opposite corners of the community: Creekside Villa at 27435 29A Ave in the core, beside Bertrand Creek, and Pioneer Park, a manufactured-home co-operative at 27111 0 Ave at the south edge by the US border.

Schools physically in Aldergrove (SD35): Parkside Centennial Elementary, 3300 270 Street; Shortreed Community Elementary, 27330 28 Avenue; Coghlan Fundamental Elementary, 4452 256 Street; North Otter Elementary, 5370 248 Street; Betty Gilbert Middle School, 26845 27 Avenue; Aldergrove Community Secondary, 26850 29 Avenue. Catchments are address-based through the SD35 School Locator.

Recreation: the Aldergrove Credit Union Community Centre, 27032 Fraser Highway, is the Township's recreation complex in Aldergrove — pools plus the Otter Co-op Outdoor Experience waterpark, an ice arena, a fitness centre and an indoor walking track. Aldergrove Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library) is at 26770 29 Avenue.

Transit: TransLink route 503 (Aldergrove/Langley – Fraser Hwy Express) runs from 272 Street at Fraser Highway via Langley Centre to Surrey Central Station; BC Transit route 21 (Aldergrove Connector) links Aldergrove with Abbotsford from the same stop. No SkyTrain or West Coast Express station is in Aldergrove, and TransLink's 503 timetable shows roughly 70 minutes end-to-end to Surrey Central on early-morning trips, stretching to about 90 minutes at peak.

Health care: Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway, Langley, is the nearest hospital confirmed on a health authority source; the long-term care home inside Aldergrove itself is Jackman Manor.
Much of the Township's land is within the Agricultural Land Reserve, and Bertrand Creek bounds the core area to the north and east — both matter to the rural lots around the 55+ complexes.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Aldergrove

items.t: Township zoning: Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500: governs Aldergrove. Its Section 110.1 zone ladder, as read out in Township council reports, runs from R-1B/R-1C urban lots at 464.5 m² minimum up to SR-2 suburban lots at 8,094 m² minimum, with rural zones beyond the core; MLS data for Creekside Villa records its zoning as RM-2.

The Township's bylaw has its own "seniors' housing" definition: a Township council report varying Zoning Bylaw 2500 for a seniors' housing project records the bylaw definition's maximum seniors' housing dwelling-unit size as 70 m² (753 ft²) — Township zoning treats seniors' housing as a defined use separate from a strata's 55+ age bylaw, and the two should not be conflated on a page.
Plans: the Aldergrove Community Plan and the Aldergrove Core Area Plan govern the community, within the Township's Official Community Plan.

ALR check before any rural-lot assumption: much of the Township's land is within the Agricultural Land Reserve, and the Township directs applicants to check a property's ALR designation and watercourses in GeoSource before applying.

Property taxes: Township of Langley property taxes and utility fees were due Thursday, July 2, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to current-year taxes unpaid at midnight July 2, 2026, with a further 5% at midnight September 3, 2026, and utility fees are now billed separately.

blocks.text: The BC rules on 55+ age bylaws, who may own and who may live in a unit, the exemptions and rentals apply in every strata and are explained once, with sources, on the BC 55+ strata rules page.

items.t: BC 55+ strata rules

Aldergrove's two 55+ ownership products run on two different legal systems. Creekside Villa is a freehold strata under the Strata Property Act (plan LMS361); Pioneer Park is a housing co-operative where you buy the home plus co-op shares and the co-op approves the buyer. Fees, resale steps and occupancy rules are not interchangeable between the two, and neither is a pad-rental park of the kind the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act governs.

The "Creekside" name is used twice in the core, for different complexes. Creekside Villa (27435 29A Ave) is the verified 55+ complex backing onto Bertrand Creek; Creekside Estates (27125 31A Ave) is a separate townhouse complex with no age restriction found in any source. A name-only search will mix them.

Old Creekside Villa listings say "45+" — that cannot be a valid strata bylaw today. One older listing called a unit a "large 45+ rancher" while recording "Restricted Age: 55+" in its property data; since Nov 24, 2022, BC strata age bylaws below 55 are invalid, so only the 55+ reading can govern.

Pioneer Park sits on 0 Avenue — the border road. Its address, 27111 0 Ave, puts the co-op at the community's south edge on the US border, a rural setting apart from the Fraser Highway core where Creekside Villa and Jackman Manor sit; the two 55+ options are not interchangeable locations.

The Township bylaw's "seniors' housing" is a zoning term, not an age bylaw. Zoning Bylaw 2500 defines seniors' housing with a maximum unit size (70 m² in the bylaw definition, per a Township council report) — a project can be zoned seniors' housing without being a 55+ strata, and Creekside Villa's 55+ status comes from its strata bylaw, not its RM-2 zoning.

The seniors housing most directories attach to "Langley" is not in Aldergrove. The Langley Lions Housing Society campus, including The Maple (101 independent seniors' homes, 5460 203rd St), is in Langley City — a buyer searching "Aldergrove seniors housing" will be shown Langley City product that is a separate community and a separate market.

Aldergrove's care home predates its 55+ strata. Jackman Manor opened in 1982, a decade before Creekside Villa was built in 1992 — the community's seniors infrastructure started with non-profit care, and the ownership downsizer product is the later addition.

faq.q: What 55+ homes can I actually buy in Aldergrove?
faq.a: Two verified ownership options: strata rancher townhouses at Creekside Villa (27435 29A Ave, 55 units, LMS361), and manufactured homes in the Pioneer Park co-operative (27111 0 Ave), where the purchase includes co-op shares and a co-op acceptance step. No 55+ rental building or subsidized complex was verified inside Aldergrove.

faq.q: How is Pioneer Park different from a normal manufactured-home park?
faq.a: It is a co-operative, not a pad-rental park: listings state the buyer must be accepted by the co-op and must purchase co-op shares ($9,200 in one listing, refunded upon sale), and pays a monthly co-op fee ($510 in the same listing) rather than pad rent to a landlord. Confirm the current figures and rules with the co-op — they are listing-stated, not a published tariff.

faq.q: Do both of us have to be 55 at Pioneer Park?
faq.a: One listing states the rule in its strictest form — "Strictly 55plus (both occupants must be 55)" — while another listing for the same park states only that the park is 55+ and that occupancy is limited to 2 occupants who are 55+. Because a co-op sets its own occupancy rules, get the co-op's current rule in writing before writing an offer; do not rely on the strata exemptions.

At Creekside Villa, MLS data records pets allowed with restrictions, and listings state 2 pets maximum with a shoulder-height limit of 14 inches. At Pioneer Park, listings state 2 pets allowed with no size restrictions. Confirm the current rule for the specific complex before writing.

faq.q: Is there long-term care in Aldergrove if I need it later?
faq.a: Yes — Jackman Manor, 27477 28 Ave, is an 88-bed long-term care home operated by the Aldergrove Lions Seniors Housing Society in partnership with Fraser Health. Admission is through Fraser Health assessment, not by purchase or market rent.

faq.q: How do I get to Surrey or Abbotsford without driving?
faq.a: TransLink route 503 runs from 272 Street at Fraser Highway to Surrey Central Station via Langley Centre (roughly 70–90 minutes end-to-end depending on time of day, per TransLink's timetable), and BC Transit route 21 connects Aldergrove with Abbotsford from the same stop. There is no SkyTrain in Aldergrove.
